title: Riposate, vezzose ragazze!
subtitle: Don Giovanni, Leporello, Zerlina, Masetto, Donna Elvira, Donna Anna and Don Ottavio: the ballroom scene of the finale from Don Giovanni, Act 1 (No. 13)

passages.label: Allegro: Riposate, vezzose ragazze! · Rinfrescatevi, bei giovinetti! · Tornerete a far presto le pazze
Ehi, Caffè! · Cioccolate! · Ah, Zerlina! giudizio! · Troppo dolce comincia la scena
Sei pur vaga, brillante Zerlina! · Sua bontà! · La briccona fa festa! · Sei pur cara · Tocca pur
Quel Masetto mi par stralunato · Qui bisogna cervello adoprar
Quel Masetto mi par stralunato (all four) · Tocca, tocca! · Ah briccona!
Maestoso: Venite pur avanti, vezzose mascherette! · È aperto a tutti quanti
Siam grati a tanti segni di generosità · È aperto a tutti, a tutti quanti
Viva la libertà! · Ricominciate il suono! (to the bar before the Minuetto)

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Don Giovanni, K. 527 (1787), Act 1 scenes 21–22 (as Castel numbers them; scene 20 in other librettos), No. 13 Finale, the ballroom from its Allegro to the bar before the Minuetto ("Meco tu dei ballare")
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Lorenzo Da Ponte, libretto of Don Giovanni (1787)
licences.author: Lorenzo Da Ponte (1749–1838)
licences.notes: Words as printed in the Schirmer vocal score, which differ from the libretto in places: bei giovinetti (libretto giovanotti); Cioccolate! (libretto Cioccolata!); Gianotta (libretto Giannotta); quest' affar printed as two words; Zerlina's added sì; Masetto's added Tocca, tocca!; Leporello's liberta in bar 121, printed without its accent. Don Giovanni's last word, ballerini, is split by the end of the piece: balle- here, -rini! on the first bar of the Minuetto.

licences.source: G. Schirmer vocal score, New York 1900 (plate 15147, IMSLP #68957), pages 127–135, bars 1–133 of the ballroom scene of No. 13 (to page 135, system 1, bar 4, the bar before the Minuetto)
licences.author: G. Schirmer, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages in two chunks (pp. 127–130, 131–135): the sung lines and the piano each read by two independent readers, every disagreement settled on the page by a judge, then checked bar by bar and checked again by fresh checkers, whose findings were corrected. Don Ottavio's part is written at sounding pitch. In bar 119 Don Giovanni's part has a second, lower note (C3) on the stem of its C4, as printed; it plays with the line. The English singing translation and the stage directions are left out. Allegro 6/8 E-flat major bars 1–87, Maestoso 2/4 C major bars 88–133. Playback tempo from complete recordings' track times: the Allegro (bars 1–87, the track "Riposate, vezzose ragazze") median 1:20 of five sets (Giulini 1959 1:18, Klemperer 1966 1:25, Barenboim 1975 1:21, Marriner 1991 1:16, I. Fischer 2026 1:20): ♩ = 196 (dotted quarter ≈ 65); the Maestoso (bars 88–133, the track "Venite pur avanti", which ends before "Ricominciate il suono!" in some sets and at the Minuetto in others) from four sets (Giulini 1:23, Muti 1990 1:37, Marriner 1:30, I. Fischer 1:28), median ♩ = 62; about 2 minutes in all. Mozart gives the words only.
